_source: Transcribed from 'Michael Omoto CV.pdf' (Drive, modified 2026-06-28). Update this file from the CV rather than editing the Work page directly.
summary: Engineering and product leader bridging Silicon Valley and Japan. Cognitive scientist by training; has built and scaled teams and shipped privacy-critical, payments, and AI products at Google, Mercari, and Presto. Has also taught and designed curriculum for over a decade, from ESL classrooms and coding bootcamps to middle-school, high-school, and university programs.

bullets: Paid advisory work, following seven years of volunteering with the same school.
Bootstrapped the product-engineering team, recruited five engineers with Silicon Valley experience in Tokyo, and set its technical direction and principles.
Founded the company's Japan entity; secured its first contracts and helped shape the go-to-market strategy.
Led the expansion of AI-driven wealth-management products for the Japanese market.
Led 21 engineers across 4 subteams owning every user-generated-content solicitation surface — Contribute Tab, Creator Zone, Notifications, Campaigns, and ML targeting — on Android and iOS.
Shipped a multi-year, privacy-by-design system for client-side, location-history-based content solicitation, removing Google's exposure to geofence warrants.
Served as location-data privacy lead, assessing risk with the central Privacy team.
Led the engineering intern program, supporting 40+ interns a year alongside internal talks and external events.
As a 20% project, served as a Computer Science Education Program Manager, partnering with nonprofits.
Member of the Japan Site DEI Tech Council.
First English-speaking engineering manager; drove the rapid internationalization of the engineering org.
Hired 100+ engineers across all seniority levels.
Owned shipping and payments for the US product.
Founded the English Developer PR program; launched Women Who Code @ Mercari and the Global Engineering Meetup.
Built engineering onboarding and a practical-engineering bootcamp for new-grad hires.
Executive sponsor of Build@Mercari, a training and internship program for people underrepresented in tech.

experience.note: formerly E la Carte · Redwood City, CA
bullets: Fourth engineering hire and first infrastructure / distributed-systems engineer; wrote most of the backend, including metrics, infrastructure, and the SaaS-management product.
Promoted to Director of Engineering in 2016; grew the org to 30+ engineers.
Owned a hardware-and-software roadmap tied to $100M+ in contract value.
Helped scale the company from Series A to D (~$200M valuation; Y Combinator-backed).
Led business development and due diligence for Japan expansion.
2017 Timmy Award nominee, Best Tech Manager (Silicon Valley).

earlier.text: Neuroscience research at the VA Medical Center — epilepsy cell-culture work under a UCLA grant, later a research coordinator routing protocols through IACUC, IRB and biosafety review. Applied behavioural therapy at Pacific Child & Family, doing ABA for children on the autism spectrum. English teaching in Japan as an Assistant Language Teacher with Heart Corporation, in Chiba and Ibaraki public schools. Consumer-science R&D at Neutrogena, where I designed and ran studies and built a web scraper and natural-language analysis engine — the first production code of a now decade-plus engineering career.

community.org: American Chamber of Commerce in Japan
bullets: Works with boards of education, the U.S. Embassy, and public and private institutions to help member companies build a globally minded, preferably bilingual talent pool.
Primary technical lead and engineer for a four-language platform — English, Japanese, Spanish, Portuguese — hosting a 20-year, daily-updated archive of Nikkei stories.
Re-platformed the site from DigitalOcean droplets to AWS on an auto-deploying stack; thousands of commits modernising and maintaining the codebase since 2018.

community.note: NPO closing Japan's IT gender gap
bullets: Proposed the programs, designed the strategy, and authored Waffle's successful application for the $600K Google.org Impact Challenge for Women and Girls grant.
Built the curriculum for both the Technovation (middle- and high-school) and Waffle College (university-level) programs.
As primary internal Google sponsor, raised $100K through giving campaigns and recruited 30+ mentors.

Helped lead the organising committee for COPANI XX (San Francisco, 2019): set conference strategy, led fundraising, and drafted the keynote invitation that helped secure former U.S. Transportation & Commerce Secretary Norman Mineta.
Seven cohorts; weekly mentoring plus whiteboarding and interview workshops.
Fireside chats, a solutions panel, and continuing volunteer involvement with the bootcamp since 2019.

education.note: Senior thesis in mathematical psychology: a Bayesian model predicting individual strength from team results.

education.credential: A.A. General Science, graduated with honours
